ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, when a circular card with a radius of \(2 \, \text{cm}\) is folded such that the arc exactly passes through the center of the circle, what is the length of the crease?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OA, and connect point O with the symmetrical point E with respect to AB, intersecting AB at point D,\\
By folding, we get $OD=DE=\frac{1}{2}OE=1\text{ cm}$, $OD\perp AB$,\\
$\therefore AD=BD=\frac{1}{2}AB$,\\
In $\triangle AOD$, $OD^2+AD^2=OA^2$,\\
$\therefore AD=\sqrt{OA^2-OD^2}=\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$,\\
$\therefore AB=2AD=2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$,\\
Hence, the length of the crease is $AB=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, when a circular card with a radius of \(2\,\text{cm}\) is folded such that the arc exactly passes through the center of the circle, what is the length of the crease?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: As shown in the figure, connect OA, and connect point O with the symmetrical point E with respect to AB, intersecting AB at point D. By folding, we get $OD=DE=\frac{1}{2}OE=1\text{ cm}$, $OD\perp AB$. $\therefore AD=BD=\frac{1}{2}AB$. In $\triangle AOD$, $OD^2+AD^2=OA^2$. $\therefore AD=\sqrt{OA^2-OD^2}=\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. $\therefore AB=2AD=2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circular card, with the center O marked inside the circle; below there is a line segment connecting two points A and B on the circumference, representing the crease AB; below AB there is a dashed arc, representing the folded circular arc, and the problem statement explains that after folding, this circular arc just passes through the center O. Reasoning: Suppose there is a point E on the original lower circular arc that is folded to the center O. Folding is symmetry with respect to the crease AB, so AB is the perpendicular bisector of OE. Because E is on the original circle and O is the center, OE equals the radius 2 cm, therefore the distance from O to the crease AB is OE/2 = 1 cm. AB is a chord in the circle, the circle radius r = 2 cm, and the distance from the center to the chord d = 1 cm, so the half-chord length is sqrt(r^2 - d^2) = sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3) cm. Thus the crease length AB = 2sqrt(3) cm.
